A commenter liked the early Klaviyo CRM. They noted it helps understand the behavior of a handful of named users, and compared it to applying the Klout methodology to CRM by ranking 'importance' to triage personal attention. Their nitpick: the blue circles in the UI are visually confusing until you realize they represent popup comments.

A user highlighted the JavaScript snippet integration: you can tag events on your site (logged in, performed action) much like Mixpanel, then use the system to act on them. They said it would be 'super simple' to set up a 'Haven't seen you in a while' email with no extra work, and that a non-technical person could add a lot of value to an existing site.
A user felt $49/month at the entry level 'seems a bit steep' and suggested Klaviyo may be pricing itself out of the market.

A startup user said the barrier was trying it out. They had already dropped Highrise and planned to drop their current CRM, but didn't want to commit until they were sure it fit their needs. They asked for a limited trial plan.
The owner of a 5-employee company said $49/month was fine, but expected about 5 user accounts at that price rather than just 1, and about 25 accounts on the $250/month package.
Another commenter disagreed with the pricing complaints. In their view, if you're hesitating on $49/month for a product like this, you're probably better served by Excel or an ad-hoc solution.
